sections.h2: Your options for selling in New Berlin
sections.html:
Three routes are open: hire an agent, sell it yourself, or take an offer from a cash buyer who accepts the property as it stands. How much repair work the house needs and how quickly you must close usually decide it. The Wisconsin rules below apply on every route.

  • List with an agent. You reach the most buyers, but they often order inspections and ask for repairs. Commission comes from your listing agreement, so get the percentage and any other charges in writing before you sign.
  • Sell it yourself. Marketing, showings and paperwork are all yours, including the condition report and the deed.
  • Take a cash offer. A cash buyer typically skips financing and repairs. Read the contract for the closing date, who pays for title work and any fee taken from your proceeds.

New Berlin sits in eastern Waukesha County within the Milwaukee metro area and has 39,953 residents. About 76.5 percent of occupied homes are lived in by their owners, and about 23.6 percent of residents are 65 or older. That often means long-held houses with decades of renovations, so collect the permit history of past work before a buyer asks.

The city's median owner-occupied home value is $365,700. It is a survey figure covering every owner-occupied home and says little about what your house will bring, which turns on condition, lot and timing.

sections.h2: Which school district serves your house
sections.html:
Four public districts reach into New Berlin: Elmbrook, Muskego-Norway, New Berlin, and West Allis-West Milwaukee. The city's Schools page names all four, along with private schools.

District also affects the tax bill. The city's Tax Levies and Rates page explains that rates vary with the school district a property sits in. Look at the district printed on your own tax bill before you talk to buyers, since many ask first which district their children would attend.

Start with Community Development on the second floor of City Hall, 3805 S. Casper Drive. The permits page says applications are taken Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, inspectors staff the front counter from 8:00 to 9:00 am on weekdays, and a building permit review can take up to 10 business days.

Buyers and their inspectors tend to check these kinds of past work against permit records:

  • Furnaces, air conditioners and water heaters, new or replacement
  • Decks, attached or detached, and accessory buildings such as garages and sheds
  • Kitchen remodels, additions, alterations and recreation rooms
  • Generators, hot tubs, pools and solar panels
  • Razing of a structure

Unsure whether earlier work was permitted? Call Community Development before you list.

Utility bills matter at closing too. Under Wis. Stat. 66.0809, a utility balance left unpaid after October 31 carries a 10 percent penalty, and an unpaid balance plus penalty may be moved onto the tax bill after November 15. Clear water, sewer and stormwater balances before you sell. Ask the assessor's office for the city's assessment calendar, which sets the notice, Open Book and Board of Review dates each year.

If you sell a one-to-four-unit home, Wis. Stat. 709.02 requires a completed Real Estate Condition Report in the buyer's hands no later than 10 days after the offer is accepted. A buyer who misses it may rescind within two business days after those 10 days and gets deposits back.

The form is a disclosure, not a warranty. Under Wis. Stat. 709.01, two groups are excused: court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the property, and transfers exempt from the real estate transfer fee. If you learn something that changes an answer after completing the report but before the buyer accepts, Wis. Stat. 709.035 calls for an amended report within 10 days of acceptance. Answer every item, because a report counts as complete only when each one is answered.

The state transfer fee is 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller under Wis. Stat. 77.22, and the register collects it when the deed is submitted. Waukesha County's fee guide says to round the price up to the next hundred first. Recording a deed adds $30 at the Waukesha County Register of Deeds.

Deed filing in Waukesha County
StepCost or ruleDetail

Deed recording$30Check or money order only, no cash, credit or debit

Questions go to 262-548-7585 or recording@waukeshacounty.gov. The office is open 8:00 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays.

Some transfers carry no fee. Wis. Stat. 77.25 exempts transfers by will, descent or survivorship, and a foreclosure deed or deed in lieu to a mortgage holder. When a spouse has died, the county's recording page points to the Termination of Decedent's Interest form (HT-110). The county does not require the tax bill or a death certificate for it.

Before you contact buyers, gather the documents a title company will ask for: the parcel number from your tax bill, your lender's payoff figure, permit records for earlier work, and your school district. Add water, sewer and stormwater account details so the final bill is clean. For a house still titled with a deceased spouse, plan on the HT-110 form together with a transfer return receipt and a copy of the document showing the interest.

Then ask each buyer or agent for the same things in writing: the closing date, the fees deducted from your proceeds and what happens if an inspection turns up a problem. That way offers can be compared on equal terms.

faqs.q: Can I sell my New Berlin house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, you can ask for an as-is sale in the contract, and many cash buyers work that way. The condition report is a separate duty, though. Unless you are exempt, you still give the buyer a completed report within 10 days of acceptance.

faqs.q: Who pays the Wisconsin transfer fee when a New Berlin home sells?
faqs.a: The seller. Wis. Stat. 77.22 puts the fee on the grantor at 30 cents per $100 of value, and the register of deeds collects it when the deed is recorded. Settle in the contract who covers any other closing charges.

faqs.q: How fast does Waukesha County return a recorded deed?
faqs.a: An e-recorded deed comes back immediately. For paper, give a valid email address and the document is returned immediately after recording, or enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope and expect it back in two to three weeks.

faqs.q: What do I file if a co-owner of my New Berlin house has died?
faqs.a: The Termination of Decedent's Interest form (HT-110), a transfer return receipt, a copy of the document showing the decedent's interest, and a $30 check or money order. Confirm with the office or an attorney for your situation.

faqs.q: Do utility bills affect my sale?
faqs.a: Yes. A utility balance left unpaid after October 31 carries a 10 percent penalty, and an unpaid balance plus penalty may be moved onto the tax bill after November 15. Clear water, sewer and stormwater charges before closing.
